text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service on Friday reaffirmed United Grain Growers Ltd debt rating as stable.

"CBRS has reaffirmed UGG unsecurited debentures at B++ (low), commercial paper at A-1 (low) and preferred shares at P-3 (low) following the withdrawal of the takeover bid for the Company by both Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators," CBRS' statement said.
Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators on February 20 launched a C$13.75 a share hostile bid for UGG, one of Canada's largest grain handlers.
They dropped their C$172 million offer Tuesday after a Manitoba court ruled UGG's poison pill had been triggered.

"Although the Manitoba court ruled on March 18th that the 'Flip-in Poison Pill Plan' was triggered, no steps have been taken to implement this defense given the bid's subsequent withdrawal. Hence, no material adverse impact on UGG's balance sheet is anticipated," CBRS' statement said.
UGG's rating outlook was reaffirmed at stable, CBRS said.
"However, we anticipate there will be associated professional fees incurred resulting from this recent defense which will impact earnings," CBRS said.
